There's a similar check in place in the OBJ importer, although it's designed to check if the file is binary instead of being text: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/editor/import/3d/resource_importer_obj.cpp#L204

It's likely possible to write this in a more robust/efficient manner, but it probably works well enough as-is.

It might be better to use `get_buffer()` or similar and then `strcmp` here as `get_8()` will likely be slower (and uncached last time I looked).

Aside from that, this looks good to me.

"empty size" is a weird thing to say. It would be better to say "empty file" or "size is zero" or similar. Or maybe just directly say it's empty (a very specific problem) instead of stating that it's corrupt (a general problem).

Also, why call it a "Resource file"? It's not imported yet, so it's technically not a Resource yet. A problem with a "Resource file" could suggest that it's a bug in Godot's importer, while it's actually a problem with the source file in the user's project.

```suggestion
			vformat("Source file is empty (0 bytes), cannot import '%s' as a Resource.", p_file));
```
Presumably you have to check here whether it's actually managed to read this number of bytes from the file? Otherwise it will crash if `buffer.ptr()` contains less than `strlen`?

I've tested it on a file smaller than 23 bytes (`strlen(sample)`) and it doesn't crash or print any error.

If I `print_line()` the buffer, I can see its contents' size will be smaller than 23 bytes, but it won't crash.

I don't think it is safe though by definition. It won't crash in every case. asan might pick this up, or `PackedByteArray` might be hiding the bug by reserving more than the size required.

Essentially `buffer` can be less than 23 bytes (in theory, even if not in practice), then you are `strcmp`ing into garbage data.

_(Alternatively you can convert both of these to Godot `Strings`, as these are safe by default. C string functions don't do any hand holding here.)_

I've tried to replace the check with your suggestion locally, but it never triggers now (even for LFS pointer files).

> Note using > condition because strlen returns size not including null terminator.

Since buffer's size is determined by `file->get_buffer(strlen(sample))`, doesn't that mean it never includes the null terminator's size? Therefore, this would mean the condition can never be `true`.
